translations.literal: The emperor, because Mengyang Pacification Commission headmen Dao Bianman and others harbored Jifa, counted their crimes in an edict, saying: "Mengyang was established by the court; you Dao Bianman and others dare defy court orders—first ground for punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding that Mengyang headmen including Dao Bianman hid Jifa, listed their offenses in an edict: "Mengyang was established by the court; you, Dao Bianman and the rest, defy imperial orders—first ground for war.

sentences.zh: 思機發系賊子，故縱不捕，二可伐。

translations.literal: Si Jifa is the son of a rebel bandit; you deliberately let him go uncaptured—second ground for punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Si Jifa is a rebel's son, yet you leave him at large—second ground for war.

sentences.zh: 爾孟養被思任發奪地，逐爾宣慰，見在雲南優養，爾等與仇為黨，三可伐。

translations.literal: Your Mengyang had lands seized by Si Lunfa and your Pacification Commissioner expelled; he is now generously maintained in Yunnan; you band with the enemy—third ground for punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lunfa took your lands and drove out your commissioner, who now lives on court charity in Yunnan; you side with the enemy—third ground for war.

sentences.zh: 雲南總兵官世世管屬爾地，奉命捕取賊子，爾等不從調度，四可伐。

translations.literal: The Yunnan regional commander-in-chief has from generation to generation governed your territory, ordered to capture the rebel bandit's son; you do not obey deployment—fourth ground for punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's regional commander has held your land for generations and was ordered to seize the rebel's son; you refuse to answer the call—fourth ground for war.

sentences.zh: 爾等不過以為山川險阻，官軍未易遽到，又以為氣候瘴癘，官軍不可久居。

translations.literal: You merely think mountains and rivers are perilously obstructive, so government troops cannot easily arrive swiftly, and also think the climate is malarial and pestilential, so government troops cannot dwell long.
translations.idiomatic: You count on rugged terrain to keep the army from reaching you quickly, and on malarial climate to keep it from staying long.

sentences.zh: 勢強則拒敵，力弱則奔遁。

translations.literal: When strength is strong then resist the enemy; when power is weak then flee and escape.
translations.idiomatic: When you are strong you stand and fight; when you are weak you run.

sentences.zh: 殊不知昔馬援遠標銅柱，險阻無傷，諸葛亮五月渡瀘，炎蒸無害，皆能破滅蠻眾，開拓境土。

translations.literal: You little know that in the past Ma Yuan set the bronze pillar far away—perilous obstacles did no harm; Zhuge Liang crossed the Lu in the fifth month—the scorching heat did no injury; all were able to destroy and exterminate the barbarian masses and open and expand border lands.
translations.idiomatic: You forget that Ma Yuan marched deep and erected his bronze pillar without fear of terrain, and that Zhuge Liang crossed the Lu River in the fifth month's heat to crush the tribes and open new lands.

sentences.zh: 況今大軍有必勝之機，麓川之師可為前鑒。

translations.literal: Moreover today the great army has a condition of certain victory; the Luchuan expedition can serve as a prior lesson.
translations.idiomatic: Today the imperial army stands on ground of certain victory, with the Luchuan campaign as a recent warning.

sentences.zh: 爾等速宜悔過自圖，令思機發親自前來，仍與一官一地，令享生全。

translations.literal: You should swiftly and properly repent and take thought for yourselves, making Si Jifa come in person; still give him one office and one territory, letting him enjoy life intact.
translations.idiomatic: Repent at once and bring Si Jifa here yourself; he will still receive an office and lands and keep his life.

sentences.zh: 如不肯出，爾等即擒為上策；

translations.literal: If unwilling to come out, you immediately capture him—this is the superior stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: If he will not come, seize him yourselves—that is best;

sentences.zh: 跡思機發所在，報與官軍捕取為中策；

translations.literal: Track where Si Jifa is located and report to government troops to capture—this is the middle stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: Or track him down and tell the army where to take him—that is second best;

sentences.zh: 若代彼支吾，令其逃匿，則並爾等剿滅，悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: If on his behalf you stall and prevaricate, letting him flee and hide, then together with you they will be exterminated—in repentance there will be no reaching it."
translations.idiomatic: If you stall for him and let him escape, you will all be destroyed together, with no chance for regret afterward."

sentences.zh: 時已三征麓川，內旨必欲生擒機發，已密諭總督王驥，又敕諭以雲南安置孟養舊宣慰刀孟賓為向導。

translations.literal: By then three expeditions against Luchuan had already been launched; the inner intent firmly sought to capture Jifa alive; the grand coordinator Wang Ji had already been secretly instructed; further, an edict instructed using the former Mengyang Pacification Commissioner Dao Mengbin settled in Yunnan as guide.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already launched three Luchuan campaigns and was determined to take Jifa alive. Wang Ji, the grand coordinator, had been secretly instructed, and Dao Mengbin, the former Mengyang commissioner living in Yunnan, was ordered to serve as guide.

sentences.zh: 及兵出窮征，機發卒遁去，不可得。

translations.literal: When troops went out to pursue to the limit, Jifa ultimately fled away and could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched to the end of pursuit, Jifa slipped away and could not be caught.

sentences.zh: 於是乃以孟養地給緬甸宣慰馬哈省管治，命捕思機發。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mengyang territory was given to Burma Pacification Commissioner Mahaseng to govern, ordering capture of Si Jifa.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang was then given to Burma's commissioner Mahaseng to govern, with orders to capture Si Jifa.

sentences.zh: 時正統十四年也。

translations.literal: The time was Zhengtong year 14.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the fourteenth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，任發之子思卜發遣使來貢，求管孟養舊地。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year 2, Lunfa's son Si Buja sent envoys coming to offer tribute, seeking to administer Mengyang's old territory.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 2, Si Buja, son of Si Lunfa, sent tribute envoys asking to recover old Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議，孟養地已與緬甸，豈可移易。

translations.literal: Court ministers deliberated: Mengyang territory had already been given to Burma—how could it be transferred and exchanged?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued that Mengyang had already been granted to Burma and could not be reassigned.

sentences.zh: 時朝命雖不許，然卜發已潛據之，即緬甸不能奪也。

translations.literal: Though the court order at the time did not permit it, yet Buja had already secretly occupied it—even Burma could not seize it back.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused, but Buja had already seized the land by stealth, and even Burma could not drive him out.

sentences.zh: 卜發死，子思洪發嗣，自天順、成化，每朝貢輒署孟養地名，儼然自有其地矣。

translations.literal: Buja died; his son Si Hongfa succeeded; from Tianshun and Chenghua, every court tribute was signed with the Mengyang place-name—as if he truly possessed the territory himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Buja died, his son Si Hongfa succeeded him. From the Tianshun and Chenghua reigns onward, every tribute memorial bore the name Mengyang, as though the land were already his.

sentences.zh: 成化中，孟養金沙江思陸發遣人貢象馬，宴賜皆如例。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, Mengyang Jinshajiang Si Lufa sent persons offering tribute of elephants and horses; banquets and rewards were all according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua, Si Lufa of Mengyang on the Jinsha River sent elephants and horses as tribute and received the usual banquet and gifts.

sentences.zh: 思陸發者，思任發之遺孽也。

translations.literal: Si Lufa was Si Lunfa's surviving remnant seed.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lufa was a surviving scion of Si Lunfa.

sentences.zh: 太監錢能鎮雲南，思陸發數以珍寶遺能，因得入貢，稱孟養金沙江思陸發，常規立功以襲祖職。

translations.literal: Eunuch Qian Neng garrisoned Yunnan; Si Lufa repeatedly with precious treasures gifted Neng; thereby he obtained permission to offer tribute, styling himself Mengyang Jinshajiang Si Lufa, constantly planning to achieve merit and inherit ancestral office.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Qian Neng held Yunnan; Si Lufa repeatedly sent him treasure, won permission to tribute, styled himself Si Lufa of Mengyang on the Jinsha, and hoped to earn honors and recover his forefathers' commission.

sentences.zh: 適孟密安撫土舍思揲侵據木邦地，爭殺累年，守臣議征之，思陸發乃請自效。

translations.literal: Just then Mengmi Pacification native assistant Sishe encroached and seized Mubang territory; contention and killing accumulated for years; frontier officials deliberated expedition against him; Si Lufa then requested to serve personally.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengmi assistant commissioner Sishe seized Mubang lands and fighting dragged on for years, frontier officials debated an expedition, and Si Lufa offered his service.

sentences.zh: 時蠻眾相傳孟密畏思陸兵，參政毛科請於總兵鎮巡官，許之。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarian masses transmitted word that Mengmi feared Si Lu's troops; participating administrator Mao Ke requested of the regional commander and inspection circuit officials—they permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor held that Mengmi feared Si Lu's forces; Administrator Mao Ke asked the regional and circuit commanders, and they agreed.

sentences.zh: 思陸兵未至，思揲解去。

translations.literal: Si Lu's troops had not yet arrived when Sishe withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: Before Si Lu's troops arrived, Sishe withdrew.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張誥議調思陸兵，令戮力捕思揲，乃遣使促之發兵。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Gao deliberated on mobilizing Si Lu's troops, ordering combined effort to capture Sishe; then dispatched envoys urging him to dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Gao decided to mobilize Si Lu's force to hunt Sishe and sent envoys urging him to march.

sentences.zh: 思陸遣大陶孟倫索領蠻兵象馬過江，倫索既過江，指鷹謂使者曰：「我曹猶此鷹，奪得土地，即管食之耳。」

translations.literal: Si Lu dispatched senior taomeng Lun Suo leading barbarian troops, elephants, and horses across the river; Lun Suo having crossed the river, pointed at a hawk and told the envoy: "We are like this hawk—when we seize land, we simply manage and eat from it."
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu sent the senior taomeng Lun Suo across the river with tribal troops, elephants, and horses. Once across, Lun Suo pointed at a hawk and told the envoy: "We are like this hawk: seize land and feed from it."

sentences.zh: 科聞之憂甚。

translations.literal: Mao Ke heard it and was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Ke heard this, he was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 時思揲令陶孟思英以兵守蠻莫。

translations.literal: At the time Sishe ordered taomeng Si Ying to hold Manmo with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sishe had taomeng Si Ying hold Manmo with troops.

sentences.zh: 孟養兵至，思英堅守不出，已而請和。

translations.literal: Mengyang troops arrived; Si Ying firmly defended and did not come out; after a time he requested peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengyang troops arrived, Si Ying held firm and refused battle, then asked for peace.

sentences.zh: 孟養兵聞官軍聽思英約降，頗有怨言。

translations.literal: Mengyang troops heard government troops heeded Si Ying's agreement to surrender and had considerable complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang's soldiers grumbled when they learned the army had accepted Si Ying's offer to surrender.

sentences.zh: 官軍糧絕，遽引退。

translations.literal: Government troops' grain was exhausted; they abruptly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Government supplies ran out and the army withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 倫索亦恐思英絕其歸路，取道幹崖而還。

translations.literal: Lun Suo also feared Si Ying would cut off his return route; he took the route through Ganya and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lun Suo, fearing Si Ying would block his retreat, returned by way of Ganya.

sentences.zh: 科念倫索前語，急戒令孟養還兵守疆界，孟養不聽。

translations.literal: Mao Ke, recalling Lun Suo's earlier words, urgently admonished and ordered Mengyang to return troops and guard the border; Mengyang would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling Lun Suo's earlier boast, Mao Ke urgently ordered Mengyang to withdraw and guard its borders, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 初，靖遠伯王驥與之約誓，非總兵官符檄不得渡江。

translations.literal: Initially, Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji made a sworn covenant with them: without the regional commander's dispatch and proclamation they could not cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji had sworn that they could not cross the river without the regional commander's written order.

sentences.zh: 自是遂犯約，數興兵過江與孟密戰。

translations.literal: From this they then violated the covenant, repeatedly raising troops across the river to fight Mengmi.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they broke the pact and repeatedly crossed the river to fight Mengmi.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年，雲南巡按謝朝宣奏：

translations.literal: In Hongzhi year 12, Yunnan touring censor Xie Chaoxuan memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 12, Yunnan touring censor Xie Chaoxuan memorialized:

sentences.zh: 孟養思陸本麓川叛種，竄居金沙江外。

translations.literal: Mengyang's Si Lu was originally of Luchuan's rebel stock, hiding and dwelling beyond the Jinsha River.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang's Si Lu was a Luchuan rebel who had fled beyond the Jinsha River.

sentences.zh: 成化中，嘗據緬甸之聽盞。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, he once occupied Burma's Tingshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua he had once seized Tingshan in Burma.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年征調其兵渡江，遂復據騰沖之蠻莫。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi year 7 his troops were conscripted and crossed the river; he then again occupied Tengchong's Manmo.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 7 his troops were mobilized across the river, and he again seized Manmo in Tengchong.

sentences.zh: 又糾木邦兵，攻燒孟密安撫司，殺掠蠻民二千余人，劫象馬金寶，有並吞孟密覬覦故土之誌。

translations.literal: He also rallied Mubang troops, attacked and burned the Mengmi Pacification Commission office, killed and plundered more than two thousand barbarian people, seized elephants, horses, gold, and treasures, and had the intent to swallow Mengmi whole and covet old territory.
translations.idiomatic: He also rallied Mubang troops, attacked and burned the Mengmi pacification office, killed and plundered more than two thousand tribespeople, seized elephants, horses, gold, and treasure, and clearly aimed to swallow Mengmi and recover his old lands.

sentences.zh: 迤西人恭們、騰沖人段和為之謀主，屢撫不聽。

translations.literal: Yixi native Gongmen and Tengchong native Duan He served as his chief plotters; repeated pacification he would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Gongmen of Yixi and Duan He of Tengchong were his chief advisers; repeated efforts at pacification failed to move him.

sentences.zh: 雲南會城去孟養遠，聲勢難接。

translations.literal: Yunnan's provincial capital is far from Mengyang; authority and momentum are hard to extend.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's provincial capital is far from Mengyang, and imperial authority there is hard to sustain.

sentences.zh: 曩於金騰添設鎮守太監，為撫蠻安民之計。

translations.literal: Formerly at Jinteng a garrison eunuch was added, as a plan to pacify the barbarians and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison eunuch had been added at Jinteng to pacify the tribes and protect the people.

sentences.zh: 而近時太監吉慶貪暴無狀，雖嘗陽卻思陸之贄，然蠻知其貪，又烏知不因其卻而更進之。

translations.literal: Yet the recent eunuch Ji Qing was greedy and violent beyond measure; though he once outwardly refused Si Lu's gifts, yet the barbarians knew his greed—who knows they did not, because of his refusal, advance gifts all the more?
translations.idiomatic: But the recent eunuch Ji Qing was flagrantly greedy and brutal; though he once publicly refused Si Lu's gifts, the tribes knew his greed and may well have offered more because he had refused.

sentences.zh: 臣聞蠻莫等處，乃水陸會通之地，蠻方器用鹹自此出，江西、雲南大理逋逃之民多赴之。

translations.literal: Your subject hears that Manmo and other places are where water and land routes meet; the barbarians' salt for daily use comes from there; fugitives from Jiangxi, Yunnan, and Dali often go there.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Manmo and the like are crossroads by land and water; salt for tribal use comes from there, and fugitives from Jiangxi, Yunnan, and Dali flock to the region.

sentences.zh: 雲南差官每多賫違禁物往彼饋送，漏我虛實，為彼腹心。

translations.literal: Yunnan dispatch officials often carry prohibited goods there to present as gifts, leaking our strengths and weaknesses and becoming their trusted insiders.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan officials often carry contraband there as gifts, betraying our strengths and weaknesses and becoming the enemy's trusted agents.

sentences.zh: 鎮夷關一巡檢耳，安能禁制。

translations.literal: Zhenyi Pass is only one inspector—how could it enforce prohibition?
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyi Pass has only a single inspector—how could it enforce control?

sentences.zh: 臣計孟養甲兵不能當中原一大縣，以雲南之勢臨之，易於壓卵。

translations.literal: Your subject reckons Mengyang's armored troops cannot match one large Central Plains county; with Yunnan's power bearing down on them, it would be easier than crushing an egg.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon Mengyang's armed force is no match for a single large Central Plains county; Yunnan's power could crush them as easily as an egg.

sentences.zh: 奈何一調即來，屢撫不退，皆鎮巡失之於初，逋逃奸人謀之於中，撫蠻中官壞之於後。

translations.literal: Yet why is it that at one summons they come, and after repeated pacification they do not withdraw? All because the regional and circuit officials failed at the start, fugitive traitors plotted in the middle, and the eunuchs who pacified the barbarians ruined matters afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they come at a single summons and refuse to withdraw despite repeated pacification—because the regional commanders failed at the outset, fugitive traitors plotted in the middle, and the pacification eunuchs ruined matters afterward.

sentences.zh: 伏望垂念邊民困苦，將雲南鎮守太監止存一員，另用指揮一員守備鎮夷關，驅思陸退歸江外，而移騰沖司於蠻莫，並木邦、孟密不得窺伺，乃為萬全之策。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes you will consider the frontier people's hardship: retain only one Yunnan garrison eunuch; separately appoint one commander to garrison Zhenyi Pass; drive Si Lu back beyond the river; move the Tengchong office to Manmo; and keep Mubang and Mengmi from watching for openings—then it would be the most secure plan.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider the frontier people's hardship: keep only one Yunnan garrison eunuch, post a commander at Zhenyi Pass, drive Si Lu back beyond the river, move the Tengchong office to Manmo, and keep Mubang and Mengmi from seizing their chance—that would be the safest course.

sentences.zh: 設思陸冥頑不聽撫諭，便當決策用兵，使無噍類，以為土官不法之戒。

translations.literal: If Si Lu is darkly stubborn and will not heed pacification and instruction, then one should resolve on using troops, leaving none to eat grain, as a warning to lawless native officials.
translations.idiomatic: If Si Lu remains obstinate and refuses pacification, then send troops and leave no survivors, as a warning to lawless native officials.

sentences.zh: 先是，吉慶已為思陸請朝貢，至是因朝宣疏，並下鎮巡官議剿撫之宜，數年不決。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ji Qing had already requested court tribute for Si Lu; when Chaoxuan's memorial arrived, both were sent down to the regional and circuit officials to deliberate whether to suppress or pacify—years passed without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ji Qing had already petitioned for Si Lu's right to tribute; when Chaoxuan's memorial arrived, both were referred to the regional commanders to decide between suppression and pacification, and years passed without resolution.

sentences.zh: 十六年，巡撫陳金乃遣金騰參將盧和撫諭思陸。

translations.literal: In year 16, Grand Coordinator Chen Jin then dispatched Jinteng assistant commander Lu He to pacify and instruct Si Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Grand Coordinator Chen Jin sent Jinteng assistant commander Lu He to negotiate with Si Lu.

sentences.zh: 和至騰沖，思陸遣陶孟投書，致方物。

translations.literal: He reached Tengchong; Si Lu dispatched a taomeng to deliver a letter and present local products.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu He reached Tengchong, Si Lu sent a taomeng with a letter and local gifts.

sentences.zh: 和諭以禍福，令掣兵過江，歸所占蠻莫等地，且調隴川、幹崖、南甸三宣撫司蠻兵及戰象，隨官軍分道至金沙江。

translations.literal: He instructed him on fortune and disaster, ordering withdrawal of troops across the river and return of occupied Manmo and other places; moreover he mobilized tribal troops and war elephants from the three pacification commissions of Longchuan, Ganya, and Nandian, following government troops by separate routes to the Jinsha River.
translations.idiomatic: Lu He warned him of reward and punishment, ordered his troops back across the river and the return of occupied Manmo and other lands, and mobilized tribal troops and war elephants from the Longchuan, Ganya, and Nandian pacification commissions to march with government forces to the Jinsha River.

sentences.zh: 思陸乃遣大陶孟倫索、怕卓等率所部來見，和等再申諭之。

translations.literal: Si Lu then dispatched senior taomeng Lun Suo, Pazhuo, and others leading their followers to come and meet; He and the others again reiterated instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu then sent senior taomeng Lun Suo, Pazhuo, and others with their followers to meet Lu He, who repeated his instructions.

sentences.zh: 思陸聽命，退還前所據蠻莫等地十三處，撤回象馬蠻兵，渡金沙江而歸。

translations.literal: Si Lu obeyed the order, returned the thirteen places previously occupied including Manmo, withdrew elephants, horses, and barbarian troops, and crossed the Jinsha River to return.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu obeyed, returned the thirteen places he had seized including Manmo, withdrew his elephants, horses, and tribal troops, and crossed the Jinsha River home.

sentences.zh: 又遣陶孟、招剛等貢象六、銀六百兩並金銀器納款。

translations.literal: He also dispatched taomeng, zhaogang, and others offering six elephants, six hundred taels of silver, and gold and silver vessels in submission.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent taomeng, zhaogang, and others with six elephants, six hundred taels of silver, and gold and silver vessels as tribute of submission.

sentences.zh: 鎮巡官以聞，並奏言：「蠻莫等地原隸木邦，成化間始為孟密所有，近又為思陸所據，連年構禍，今始平定。

translations.literal: The regional and circuit officials reported upward and jointly memorialized: "Manmo and other places originally belonged to Mubang; in the Chenghua period they first came into Mengmi's possession; recently they were again occupied by Si Lu; year after year they stirred trouble—only now is it settled.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commanders reported and jointly memorialized: "Manmo and the like originally belonged to Mubang; in Chenghua they passed to Mengmi, and recently Si Lu seized them; trouble continued for years until now.

sentences.zh: 既不可復與木邦、孟密，又不可割畀隴川、幹崖、南甸三宣撫，宜暫於騰沖歲檄官軍四百分番守之。

translations.literal: Since they cannot be returned to Mubang and Mengmi, nor carved out and given to the three pacification commissions of Longchuan, Ganya, and Nandian, it is fitting temporarily at Tengchong to dispatch four hundred government troops in rotating shifts to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot be returned to Mubang or Mengmi, nor given to the Longchuan, Ganya, and Nandian pacification commissions; Tengchong should temporarily rotate four hundred government troops to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 思陸前有助平思揲功，今悔禍納款，請賜以名目、冠帶，仍降敕獎諭。」

translations.literal: Si Lu earlier had merit in helping pacify Sishe; now repenting of disaster and submitting, he requests bestowal of title and official cap and sash; further grant an edict of reward and instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu earlier helped defeat Sishe; now repentant and submitting, he asks for an official title and cap and sash, and an edict of commendation."

sentences.zh: 部議以蠻莫等處本木邦分地，在大義宜歸之木邦。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that Manmo and other places were originally Mubang's allotted lands; in great principle they should be returned to Mubang.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry held that Manmo and the like were originally Mubang territory and in principle should be returned to Mubang.

sentences.zh: 其名目、冠帶，貢使已言思陸不願受，不宜輕畀，請賜敕厚勞遣歸之。

translations.literal: As for title and cap and sash, the tribute envoy had already said Si Lu was unwilling to receive them—they should not be lightly granted; request bestowal of an edict with generous reward and send him home.
translations.idiomatic: As for title and cap and sash, the envoy said Si Lu did not want them and they should not be granted lightly; grant an edict with generous reward and send him home.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Reply: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The reply approved it.

sentences.zh: 時思陸覬得宣慰司印，部執不予，於是仍數出兵與木邦、孟密仇殺無寧歲。

translations.literal: At the time Si Lu coveted obtaining the Pacification Commission seal; the ministry firmly withheld it; thereupon he still repeatedly dispatched troops to feud and kill with Mubang and Mengmi, with no year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu coveted the pacification commission seal, but the ministry refused; he then repeatedly sent troops to feud with Mubang and Mengmi, and peace never returned.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，總兵官沐紹勛、巡撫歐陽重遣參政王汝舟等遍歷諸蠻，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year 7, regional commander Mu Shaoxun and Grand Coordinator Ouyang Chong dispatched participating administrator Wang Ruzhou and others to tour all the barbarian domains, instructing them on fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 7, regional commander Mu Shaoxun and Grand Coordinator Ouyang Chong sent Administrator Wang Ruzhou and others to visit all the tribal domains and warn them of reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 孟養思倫等各願貢象牙、土錦、金銀器，退地贖罪。

translations.literal: Mengyang's Si Lun and others each wished to offer tribute of ivory, native brocade, and gold and silver vessels, withdrawing territory to redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lun of Mengyang and others each offered ivory, native brocade, and gold and silver vessels, ceding land to atone for their offenses.

sentences.zh: 乃以蠻莫等十三處地方寬廣，諸蠻歷年所爭，屬之騰沖司，檄軍輪守，則煙瘴可虞；

translations.literal: Since Manmo and the other thirteen places were broad in territory and what the various barbarians had fought over for years, if assigned to the Tengchong office with troops rotated by dispatch to garrison them, malarial miasma would be a concern;
translations.idiomatic: Manmo and the other thirteen places were broad and long disputed; if assigned to Tengchong with rotating garrisons, malarial sickness would be a concern;

sentences.zh: 屬之木邦，則地勢遼遠，蠻心不順。

translations.literal: If assigned to Mubang, the terrain was distant and vast, and barbarian hearts would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: if assigned to Mubang, the distance was too great and the tribes would not submit.

sentences.zh: 莫若仍屬孟密管領，歲征差發銀一千兩，而割孟乃等七處仍歸木邦罕烈，則分願均而忿爭息矣。

translations.literal: Better to leave them under Mengmi's administration, levying one thousand taels of silver annually for corvée dispatch, while carving out Mengnai and six other places to return to Mubang's Han Lie—then shares of desire would be equal and angry contention would cease.
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave them under Mengmi, levy one thousand taels of silver annually for corvée, and return Mengnai and six other places to Han Lie of Mubang—then each side would be satisfied and the feuding would end.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Reply: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The reply approved it.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年，雲南巡按陳文燧言，孟養思個與緬世仇，今更歸順於緬。

translations.literal: In Wanli year 5, Yunnan touring censor Chen Wensui said: Mengyang's Si Ge and Burma are hereditary foes; now he has turned to submit to Burma.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 5, Yunnan touring censor Chen Wensui reported that Si Ge of Mengyang, Burma's hereditary enemy, had now submitted to Burma.

sentences.zh: 因引弘治朝先臣劉健嘗議孟養事狀，謂思陸有官猶可制，即無官，其僭自若也，不如因而官之以抗緬。

translations.literal: He cited former minister Liu Jian of the Hongzhi reign, who had once deliberated on Mengyang affairs, saying: when Si Lu had an office he could still be controlled; even without an office, he usurped as before—better therefore to grant him office accordingly to resist Burma.
translations.idiomatic: He cited former minister Liu Jian's Hongzhi deliberations on Mengyang: Si Lu could be controlled while he held office, yet even without one he acted as he pleased—better to appoint him officially and use him against Burma.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Reply: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The reply approved it.

sentences.zh: 十一年，緬為遊擊劉綎所敗，孟養思威亦殺緬使降於綎。

translations.literal: In year 11, Burma was defeated by mobile corps commander Liu Ting; Mengyang's Si Wei also killed Burma's envoy and surrendered to Ting.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Burma was defeated by mobile corps commander Liu Ting; Si Wei of Mengyang also killed a Burmese envoy and submitted to Liu Ting.

sentences.zh: 十三年，隴川平，乃於孟養立長官司。

translations.literal: In year 13, Longchuan was pacified; then a chief office was established at Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, after Longchuan was pacified, a chief office was established in Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，長官思真復為緬所擄，部長思遠奉思真妻來歸，給以冠帶，令歸守。

translations.literal: Before long, Chief Si Zhen was again captured by Burma; department head Si Yuan escorted Si Zhen's wife to return; cap and sash were granted, ordering him to return and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chief Si Zhen was captured again by Burma; department head Si Yuan brought Si Zhen's wife back, was granted cap and sash, and ordered to return and hold the post.

sentences.zh: 思遠乘亂自立為宣慰，貢象進方物。

translations.literal: Si Yuan seized the disorder to establish himself as Pacification Commissioner, offering elephants and presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Si Yuan seized the chaos to declare himself pacification commissioner and sent elephants and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 然遠暴虐，諸部恨之，引緬兵至，聲言還思真，思遠奔盞西。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan was brutal and tyrannical; the various tribes hated him; they brought Burmese troops, proclaiming they would restore Si Zhen; Si Yuan fled to Zhanxi.
translations.idiomatic: But Yuan was brutal, and the tribes hated him; they brought Burmese troops, claiming they would restore Si Zhen, and Si Yuan fled to Zhanxi.

sentences.zh: 有思轟者，內附，與蠻莫酋思正共據險抗緬。

translations.literal: There was one Si Hong who submitted inwardly; with Manmo chieftain Si Zheng he jointly held perilous ground to resist Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Si Hong submitted to the court and, with Manmo chieftain Si Zheng, held the high ground against Burma.

sentences.zh: 三十年，緬攻思正，轟率兵倍道馳救，至則正已被殺。

translations.literal: In year 30, Burma attacked Si Zheng; Hong led troops by double march to rush to rescue; when he arrived, Zheng had already been killed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 Burma attacked Si Zheng; Hong marched at forced pace to rescue him, but arrived after Zheng had already been killed.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，緬攻入迤西，轟走死，緬以頭目思華守其地。

translations.literal: In year 32, Burma attacked into Yixi; Hong fled and died; Burma placed headman Si Hua to guard the territory.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 Burma invaded Yixi; Hong fled and died, and Burma placed headman Si Hua to hold the land.

sentences.zh: 華死，妻怕氏代理。

translations.literal: Hua died; his wife the Pa clan acted as proxy.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua died, his wife of the Pa clan acted in his stead.

sentences.zh: 緬人更番戍守，連年征發，從行甚苦，曰：「孟養不亡，蠻何得至此！」

translations.literal: Burmese men rotated in garrison duty; year after year corvée was levied; those who followed on campaign suffered greatly, saying: "If Mengyang had not perished, how could the barbarians have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Burmese troops rotated in garrison; corvée was levied year after year, and those who marched suffered greatly, saying: "If Mengyang had not fallen, how could the tribes have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 轟之後曰放思祖，有眾千余，不敢歸，寄食於幹崖雲。

translations.literal: After Hong there was one called Fang Sizu, with more than a thousand followers; he dared not return and lived as a guest dependent at Ganya Yun.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong came Fang Sizu, with more than a thousand followers; he dared not return and lived as a dependent at Ganya Yun.

sentences.zh: 舊制，宣慰遣人俱稱頭目，唯木邦及緬甸又有陶孟及招剛等稱，孟養又有招八稱，皆見於奏章，因其俗不改。

translations.literal: By old regulation, all persons dispatched by pacification commissioners were styled headmen; only Mubang and Burma also had titles such as taomeng and zhaogang; Mengyang also had the title zhaoba—all appear in memorials, and because of their customs they were not changed.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, pacification commissioners' envoys were all styled headmen; Mubang and Burma also used titles such as taomeng and zhaogang, and Mengyang used zhaoba—all appear in memorials and were kept according to custom.

sentences.zh: 車裏，即古產裏，為倭泥、貂黨諸蠻雜居之地，古不通中國。

translations.literal: Cheli—that is, ancient Chanli—was land where the Woni, Diaodang, and various barbarians lived mixed together; anciently it did not connect with China.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli, ancient Chanli, was a region where the Woni, Diaodang, and other tribes lived mixed together and had no ancient contact with China.

sentences.zh: 元世祖命將兀良吉禋伐交阯，經所部，降之，置撒裏路軍民總管府，領六甸，後又置耿凍路耿當、孟弄二州。

translations.literal: Yuan Shizu ordered the general Uriangqadai to campaign against Jiaozhi; passing through this territory, he subdued it and established the Sali Circuit Military-Civilian General Administration Office, governing six districts; later he also established Gengdong Circuit's Gengdang and Mengnong two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai ordered the general Uriangqadai to campaign against Jiaozhi; passing through the region he subdued it and established the Sali Circuit Military-Civilian General Administration, governing six districts, and later added the Gengdang and Mengnong prefectures of Gengdong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年，蠻長刀坎來降，改置車裏軍民府，以坎為知府。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 15, the barbarian chief Dao Kan came to surrender; Cheli Military-Civilian Prefecture was re-established, with Kan as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 15 the tribal chief Dao Kan submitted; Cheli Military-Civilian Prefecture was established with Kan as prefect.

sentences.zh: 坎遣侄豐祿貢方物，詔賜刀坎及使人衣服、綺幣甚厚，以初奉貢來朝故也。

translations.literal: Kan dispatched his nephew Feng Lu to offer local products; an edict bestowed on Dao Kan and the envoys clothing and fine silks very generously, because it was their first tribute mission to court.
translations.idiomatic: Kan sent his nephew Feng Lu with local tribute; the court granted Dao Kan and his envoys lavish clothing and fine silks because this was their first mission to court.

sentences.zh: 十七年復遣其子刀思拂來貢，賜坎冠帶、鈔幣，改置軍民宣慰使司，以坎為使。

translations.literal: In year 17 he again dispatched his son Dao Sifu to offer tribute; Kan was granted cap and sash and paper money; the Military-Civilian Pacification Commission was re-established, with Kan as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he sent his son Dao Sifu with tribute; Kan received cap and sash and paper money, and the Military-Civilian Pacification Commission was established with Kan as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，子刀暹答嗣，遣人貢象及方物。

translations.literal: In year 24, his son Dao Xianda succeeded and dispatched persons offering elephants and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 his son Dao Xianda succeeded and sent elephants and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十八年以賜誥命謝恩，予賜皆如例。

translations.literal: In year 28, because of the bestowed patent of appointment, he offered thanks for grace; grants and rewards were all according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he sent thanks for the granted patent of appointment and received the usual rewards.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，刀暹答令其下剽掠威遠知州刀算黨及民人以歸。

translations.literal: In Yongle 1, Dao Xianda ordered his subordinates to raid and carry off Weiyuan prefect Dao Suandang and the people and return.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 Dao Xianda had his men raid Weiyuan and carry off Prefect Dao Suandang and his people.

sentences.zh: 西平侯沐晟請發兵討，帝命晟移文諭之，如不悛，即以兵繼。

translations.literal: Western Pacification Marquis Mu Sheng requested dispatch of troops to punish; the emperor ordered Sheng send a written proclamation instructing him; if he did not repent, then follow with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Western Pacification Marquis Mu Sheng asked to send troops; the emperor ordered him to send a written warning, and if Xianda did not repent, to follow with force.

sentences.zh: 又以車裏已納威遠印，是悔過之心已萌，不必加兵。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Cheli had already surrendered the Weiyuan seal, this showed the heart of repentance had already sprouted—there was no need to add troops.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Cheli had already returned the Weiyuan seal, showing repentance had already begun, so force was unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 晟使至，暹答果懼，還刀算黨及威遠之地，遣人貢馬謝罪。

translations.literal: When Sheng's envoy arrived, Xianda truly feared; he returned Dao Suandang and Weiyuan territory, dispatched persons offering horses to apologize for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Sheng's envoy arrived, Xianda was afraid; he returned Dao Suandang and Weiyuan territory and sent horses in apology.

sentences.zh: 帝以其能改過，宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he could reform his faults, pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him for showing repentance.

sentences.zh: 自是頻入貢。

translations.literal: From this he frequently came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he sent tribute frequently.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣內官往車裏者，道經八百大甸，為宣慰刀招散所阻。

translations.literal: When the court dispatched inner officials toward Cheli, the route passed Babai Dadian and was blocked by Pacification Commissioner Dao Zhaosan.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent inner officials to Cheli, their route through Babai Dadian was blocked by Pacification Commissioner Dao Zhaosan.

sentences.zh: 三年，刀暹答遣使請舉兵攻八百，帝嘉其忠。

translations.literal: In year 3, Dao Xianda dispatched envoys requesting to raise troops and attack Babai; the emperor praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Dao Xianda sent envoys asking to raise troops against Babai, and the emperor praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 八百伏罪，敕車裏班師，復加獎勞。

translations.literal: Babai submitted in guilt; an edict ordered Cheli to withdraw the army, and rewards and commendation were again added.
translations.idiomatic: Babai submitted; the court ordered Cheli to withdraw its army and granted further rewards.

sentences.zh: 四年遣子刀典入國學，實陰自納質。

translations.literal: In year 4 he dispatched his son Dao Dian to enter the National University—in fact secretly offering himself as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he sent his son Dao Dian to the Imperial University, in effect secretly sending a hostage.

sentences.zh: 帝知其隱，賜衣幣慰諭遣還，以道里遼遠，命三年一貢，著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor knew his hidden motive, bestowed clothing and silks to comfort and instruct and sent him back; because the route was vast and remote, he ordered tribute once every three years and established this as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood his intent, rewarded him with clothing and silks, and sent him home; because the route was so distant, he ordered tribute once every three years and made this the rule.

sentences.zh: 十一年，暹答卒。

translations.literal: In year 11, Xianda died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Xianda died.

sentences.zh: 長子刀更孟自立，驕狠失民心，未幾亦卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Dao Gengmeng established himself; arrogant and fierce, he lost the people's hearts, and before long he too died.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Dao Gengmeng seized power; arrogant and harsh, he lost popular support and soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 更孟長子霸羨年幼，眾推刀賽署司事。

translations.literal: Gengmeng's eldest son Bazhan was young; the multitude pushed Dao Sai to administer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gengmeng's eldest son Bazhan was still young, so the people put Dao Sai in charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 刀賽者，更孟弟刀怕漢也。

translations.literal: Dao Sai was Gengmeng's younger brother Dao Pahan.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Sai was Gengmeng's younger brother Dao Pahan.

sentences.zh: 怕漢死，妻以前夫子刀弄冒為暹答孫，請襲。

translations.literal: When Pahan died, his wife falsely claimed her former husband's son Dao Nong was Xianda's grandson and requested succession.
translations.idiomatic: After Pahan died, his wife falsely claimed her stepson Dao Nong was Xianda's grandson and petitioned for succession.

sentences.zh: 十五年命刀弄襲宣慰使，以更孟從弟刀雙孟為本司同知。

translations.literal: In year 15 he was ordered to appoint Dao Nong to inherit the pacification commissioner post, with Gengmeng's younger cousin Dao Shuangmeng as vice commissioner of this commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the court appointed Dao Nong pacification commissioner and made Gengmeng's cousin Dao Shuangmeng vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十九年，雙孟言刀弄屢以兵侵劫蠻民，乞別設治所，以撫其眾。

translations.literal: In year 19, Shuangmeng said Dao Nong repeatedly used troops to raid and plunder tribal people, and begged to set up a separate administrative seat to pacify the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 Shuangmeng reported that Dao Nong had repeatedly raided tribal subjects and asked for a separate administrative seat to govern them.

sentences.zh: 詔分其地，置靖安宣慰使司，升雙孟為宣慰使，命禮部鑄印給之。

translations.literal: An edict divided their territory and established the Jing'an Pacification Commission, promoted Shuangmeng to pacification commissioner, and ordered the Ministry of Rites to cast a seal and grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The court divided the territory, established the Jing'an Pacification Commission, promoted Shuangmeng to pacification commissioner, and had the Ministry of Rites cast and issue a seal.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年，雲南布政司奏刀弄、雙孟相仇殺，弄棄地投老撾，請差官招撫。

translations.literal: In Xuande year 3, the Yunnan Provincial Administration memorialized that Dao Nong and Shuangmeng were mutually feuding and killing, that Nong had abandoned the land and fled to Laos, and requested dispatch of officials to summon and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 3 the Yunnan Provincial Administration reported that Dao Nong and Shuangmeng were at feud, that Nong had abandoned his territory and fled to Laos, and asked that officials be sent to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 帝命黔國公計議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Prince of Qian to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Prince of Qian to investigate.

sentences.zh: 六年，黔國公奏，謂奉命招撫刀弄，其母具言布政司差官劉亨征差發金，亨已取去，本司復來征，蠻民因而激變逐弄，弄逃入老撾，尋還境內以死。

translations.literal: In year 6 the Prince of Qian memorialized, saying that on orders to summon and pacify Dao Nong, his mother fully stated that the Provincial Administration's dispatched official Liu Heng had levied corvée gold; Heng had already taken it, and the commission again came to levy, so the tribal people were stirred to revolt and drove Nong away; Nong fled into Laos and soon returned within the borders and died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 the Prince of Qian reported that while summoning Dao Nong, Nong's mother explained that Provincial Administration envoy Liu Heng had levied corvée gold, taken payment, and then returned to levy again, provoking a tribal uprising that drove Nong out; Nong fled to Laos, then returned to die within the borders.

sentences.zh: 未嘗棄地外投，亦未嘗與雙孟仇殺。

translations.literal: He had never abandoned the land and fled abroad, nor had he ever feuded and killed with Shuangmeng.
translations.idiomatic: He had never abandoned his territory to flee abroad, nor had he feuded with Shuangmeng.

sentences.zh: 帝命法司執劉亨等罪之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the judicial offices to arrest Liu Heng and the others and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the judicial authorities to punish Liu Heng and the others.

sentences.zh: 七年，車裏土舍刀霸羨請襲，許之，遣行人陸塤賫敕賜冠帶、襲衣。

translations.literal: In year 7, Cheli local chief Dao Bazhan requested succession; this was granted, and the courier Lu Xun was dispatched bearing an edict bestowing cap and sash and investiture robes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Cheli local chief Dao Bazhan petitioned for succession; the court approved and sent courier Lu Xun with an edict granting cap, sash, and investiture robes.

sentences.zh: 九年，靖安宣慰刀霸供言：「靖安原車裏地，今析為二，致有爭端，乞仍並為一，歲貢如例。」

translations.literal: In year 9, Jing'an Pacification Commissioner Dao Bagong said: "Jing'an was originally Cheli territory; now it has been split in two, causing disputes; I beg that it again be merged into one, with annual tribute as before."
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 Jing'an Pacification Commissioner Dao Bagong said: "Jing'an was originally Cheli land; now split in two it breeds conflict; I ask that it be reunited, with annual tribute as before."

sentences.zh: 帝從其請，革靖安宣慰，仍歸車裏，命刀霸供、刀霸羨共為宣慰使，俾上所授靖安宣慰司印。

translations.literal: The emperor granted his request, abolished the Jing'an pacification commissioner, and returned the territory to Cheli; he ordered Dao Bagong and Dao Bazhan jointly to serve as pacification commissioners and to surrender the seal granted to the Jing'an Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, abolished the Jing'an commission, restored the land to Cheli, and appointed Dao Bagong and Dao Bazhan joint pacification commissioners, requiring them to return the Jing'an seal.

sentences.zh: 正統五年命貢使賫敕及綺帛歸賜刀霸羨及妻，嘉其勤修職貢也。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong year 5 the tribute envoys were ordered to carry an edict and fine silks back to bestow on Dao Bazhan and his wife, commending their diligence in maintaining tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 5 tribute envoys were sent back with an edict and fine silks for Dao Bazhan and his wife, commending their faithful tribute service.

sentences.zh: 六年，麓川宣慰思倫發叛，詔給車裏信符、金牌，命合兵剿賊。

translations.literal: In year 6, Luchuan Pacification Commissioner Si Lunfa rebelled; an edict granted Cheli credentials and a gold tally and ordered joint troops to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Luchuan Pacification Commissioner Si Lunfa rebelled; the court issued Cheli credentials and a gold tally and ordered a joint campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年以刀霸羨奉調有功，免其積欠差發金。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year 3, because Dao Bazhan had meritorious service when called to duty, his accumulated arrears of corvée gold were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 3 Dao Bazhan's meritorious service on campaign earned remission of his accumulated corvée arrears.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，總兵官沐璘奏：「刀霸羨自殺，弟板雅忠等已推兄三寶歷代承職。

translations.literal: In Tianshun 1, Commander-in-Chief Mu Lin memorialized: "Dao Bazhan killed himself; his younger brother Ban Yazhong and the others have already pushed their elder brother Sanbao Lidai to succeed through the generations in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1 Commander Mu Lin reported: "Dao Bazhan killed himself; his brother Ban Yazhong and others had already installed their elder brother Sanbao Lidai as successor.

sentences.zh: 今板雅忠又作亂，糾合八百相仇殺。」

translations.literal: Now Ban Yazhong has again raised rebellion, gathering Babai to mutually feud and kill."
translations.idiomatic: Now Ban Yazhong has rebelled again, rallying Babai in mutual bloodshed."

sentences.zh: 帝命璘亟為撫諭，並勘奏應襲者。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Lin urgently to pacify and instruct them, and also to investigate and memorialize who should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Mu Lin to pacify them at once and report who should inherit.

sentences.zh: 二年，帝以三寶歷代者，雖刀更孟之子，乃庶孽奪嫡，謀害刀霸羨，致板雅忠借兵攻殺，不當襲。

translations.literal: In year 2 the emperor held that Sanbao Lidai, though a son of Dao Gengmeng, was a bastard who usurped the legitimate heir, plotted to kill Dao Bazhan, and caused Ban Yazhong to borrow troops to attack and kill—he ought not to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 the emperor ruled that Sanbao Lidai, though Gengmeng's son, was a usurping bastard who had plotted to kill Bazhan and provoked Ban Yazhong's armed attack, and was unfit to inherit.

sentences.zh: 但蠻民推立，姑從眾願，命襲宣慰使。

translations.literal: But because the tribal people had pushed and established him, for the moment the multitude's wish was followed, and he was ordered to inherit the pacification commissioner post.
translations.idiomatic: But since the tribes had chosen him, the court provisionally acceded to their wish and appointed him pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 成化十六年，交阯黎灝叛，頒偽敕於車裏，期會兵共攻八百，車裏持兩端。

translations.literal: In Chenghua year 16, Jiaozhi's Li Hao rebelled, issued a forged edict to Cheli, and set a date to join forces and together attack Babai; Cheli held to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 16 the Jiaozhi rebel Li Hao sent a forged edict to Cheli proposing a joint attack on Babai; Cheli hedged between both sides.

sentences.zh: 雲南守臣以聞，遣使敕車裏諸土官互相保障，勿懷二心。

translations.literal: The Yunnan border officials reported it and dispatched envoys with an edict instructing the Cheli chieftains mutually to protect and guarantee one another and not to harbor divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan officials reported this and sent envoys instructing Cheli chiefs to protect one another and remain loyal.

sentences.zh: 二十年復敕車裏等部，懼固封疆，防交人入寇，不得輕與文移，啟釁納侮。

translations.literal: In year 20 an edict was again sent to Cheli and the other departments: fearfully secure the borders, guard against Jiaozhi people entering to raid, and do not lightly exchange documents—provoking quarrels and inviting insult.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 the court again instructed Cheli and neighboring departments to hold their borders, guard against Jiaozhi incursions, and avoid correspondence that might provoke conflict.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年，緬酋莽應裏據擺古，蠶食諸蠻。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year 11, the Burmese chieftain Mang Yingli occupied Baigu and gradually encroached upon the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 11 Burmese chief Mang Yingli seized Baigu and gradually swallowed neighboring tribes.

sentences.zh: 車裏宣慰刀糯猛折而入緬，有大、小車裏之稱，以大車裏應緬，而以小車裏應中國。

translations.literal: Cheli Pacification Commissioner Dao Nuomeng submitted and entered Burma; there came to be the names Great and Little Cheli—Great Cheli answering to Burma, and Little Cheli answering to China.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli Pacification Commissioner Dao Nuomeng submitted to Burma, and the region came to be called Great and Little Cheli—Great Cheli answering to Burma and Little Cheli to China.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十三年命元江土舍那恕往招，糯猛復歸，獻馴象、金屏、象齒諸物，謝罪。

translations.literal: In Wanli year 13 he was ordered to send Yuanjiang local chief Na Shu to summon him; Nuomeng returned, offered tamed elephants, gold screens, ivory, and other goods, and apologized for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 13 the court sent Yuanjiang chief Na Shu to summon him; Nuomeng returned with tamed elephants, gold screens, ivory, and other gifts in apology.

sentences.zh: 詔受之，聽復職。

translations.literal: An edict accepted them and permitted restoration to office.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his submission and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 天啟七年，巡撫閔洪學奏，緬人侵孟艮，孟艮就車裏求救，宣慰刀韞猛遣兵象萬余赴之。

translations.literal: In Tianqi year 7, Grand Coordinator Min Hongxue memorialized that the Burmese invaded Menggen; Menggen sought rescue from Cheli, and Pacification Commissioner Dao Wenmeng dispatched more than ten thousand troops and elephants to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year 7 Grand Coordinator Min Hongxue reported that Burmese forces invaded Menggen; Menggen appealed to Cheli, and Pacification Commissioner Dao Wenmeng sent more than ten thousand troops and elephants to help.

sentences.zh: 緬人以是恨車裏，興兵報復，韞猛年已衰，重賂求和。

translations.literal: Because of this the Burmese resented Cheli and raised troops in reprisal; Wenmeng was already old in years and heavily bribed to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: Burmese resentment led to reprisals against Cheli; Wenmeng, now aged, paid heavy bribes to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 緬聞韞猛子召河璇有女名召烏岡色美，責獻烏岡。

translations.literal: The Burmese heard that Wenmeng's son Zhao Hexuan had a daughter named Zhao Wugang of beautiful color and demanded that Wugang be presented.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wenmeng's son Zhao Hexuan had a beautiful daughter named Zhao Wugang, the Burmese demanded her surrender.

sentences.zh: 河璇別以女紿之。

translations.literal: Hexuan separately used another daughter to deceive them.
translations.idiomatic: Hexuan sent another daughter in her place to deceive them.

sentences.zh: 緬知其詐，大憤，攻車裏愈急。

translations.literal: The Burmese knew of the fraud and were greatly enraged; their attack on Cheli grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Burmese discovered the deception they were furious and pressed the attack on Cheli ever harder.

sentences.zh: 韞猛父子不能支，遁至思毛地，緬追執之以去。

translations.literal: Wenmeng, father and son, could not hold out; they fled to Simao territory, and the Burmese pursued, seized them, and took them away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenmeng and his son could not hold out; they fled to Simao, where the Burmese pursued and captured them.

sentences.zh: 中朝不及問，車裏遂亡。

translations.literal: The central court had no time to inquire; Cheli thereupon perished.
translations.idiomatic: The court could not intervene in time, and Cheli was lost.

sentences.zh: 老撾，俗呼為撾家，古不通中國。

translations.literal: Laos—commonly called Zhuojia—anciently did not connect with China.
translations.idiomatic: Laos, commonly called Zhuojia, had no ancient contact with China.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，老撾土官刀線歹貢方物，始置老撾軍民宣慰使司。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu emperor took the throne, the Laos tribal official Dao Xiandai offered local products, and the Laos Military-Civilian Pacification Commission was first established.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle emperor took the throne, Laos chief Dao Xiandai sent tribute, and the Laos Military-Civilian Pacification Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年以刀線歹為宣慰使，給之印。

translations.literal: In Yongle year 2 Dao Xiandai was made pacification commissioner and granted a seal.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2 Dao Xiandai was appointed pacification commissioner and given an official seal.

sentences.zh: 五年遣人來貢。

translations.literal: In year 5 he dispatched persons to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 既而帝以刀線歹潛通安南季犛，遣使詰責，諭其悔過。

translations.literal: Soon after, because the emperor knew Dao Xiandai had secretly communicated with Annam's Ji Li, he dispatched envoys to interrogate and rebuke him and instruct him to repent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, learning that Dao Xiandai had secretly communicated with Annam's Ji Li, the emperor sent envoys to rebuke him and demand repentance.

sentences.zh: 六年，刀線歹遣人貢象馬、方物。

translations.literal: In year 6, Dao Xiandai dispatched persons offering elephants, horses, and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Dao Xiandai sent elephants, horses, and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年復進金銀器、犀象、方物謝罪。

translations.literal: In year 7 he again presented gold and silver vessels, rhinoceroses and elephants, and local products to apologize for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he again sent gold and silver vessels, rhinoceroses, elephants, and local goods in apology.

sentences.zh: 自是連年入貢，皆賚予如例。

translations.literal: From this he came year after year to offer tribute, and all were granted rewards according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he sent tribute annually and received the usual rewards.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官楊琳往賜文綺。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the eunuch Yang Lin to go and bestow patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuch Yang Lin to bestow fine silks.

sentences.zh: 十年來貢，命禮部加賜焉。

translations.literal: In year 10 he came to offer tribute; the Ministry of Rites was ordered to add further bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: When he sent tribute in year 10, the Ministry of Rites was ordered to grant additional rewards.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年遣使賫敕獎諭宣慰刀線達。

translations.literal: In Xuande year 6 envoys were dispatched bearing an edict to commend and instruct Pacification Commissioner Dao Xianda.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 6 envoys were sent with an edict commending Pacification Commissioner Dao Xianda.

sentences.zh: 九年，老撾貢使還，恐道中為他部所阻，給信符，敕孟艮、車裏諸部遣人護之。

translations.literal: In year 9, as the Laos tribute envoys were returning, fearing they might be blocked on the route by other departments, credentials were granted, and Menggen, Cheli, and the other departments were ordered to dispatch persons to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, fearing Laos tribute envoys might be blocked en route, the court issued travel credentials and ordered Menggen, Cheli, and other departments to escort them.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年請賜土官衣服。

translations.literal: In Jingtai 1 he requested bestowal of native-official clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 he requested official clothing for the tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 故事，無加賜衣服者，命加賜錦幣並及其妻。

translations.literal: By precedent there was no additional bestowal of clothing; an order was issued to add bestowal of brocade silks, including for his wife as well.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent did not allow extra clothing grants, but the court ordered additional brocade silks for the commissioner and his wife.

sentences.zh: 成化元年頒金牌、信符於老撾。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 1 gold tallies and credentials were issued to Laos.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 gold tallies and credentials were issued to Laos.

sentences.zh: 七年鑄給老撾軍民宣慰使司印，以皆為賊焚毀也。

translations.literal: In year 7 a seal was cast and granted to the Laos Military-Civilian Pacification Commission, because all had been burned and destroyed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 a new seal was cast for the Laos Military-Civilian Pacification Commission after bandits had burned the old ones.

sentences.zh: 十六年，貢使至，會安南攻老撾，鎮守內官錢能以聞。

translations.literal: In year 16 the tribute envoys arrived just as Annam was attacking Laos; the garrison eunuch Qian Neng reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 tribute envoys arrived while Annam was attacking Laos; garrison eunuch Qian Neng reported it.

sentences.zh: 因敕其使兼程回，並量給道里費。

translations.literal: Accordingly their envoys were ordered to return by forced march, and travel expenses were also granted in measured amount.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the envoys to return at once and granted travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 明年，安南黎灝率兵九萬，開山為三道，進兵破哀牢，入老撾境，殺宣慰刀板雅及其子二人。

translations.literal: The next year, Annam's Li Hao led ninety thousand troops, opened mountains into three routes, advanced troops to break Ailao, entered Laos territory, and killed Pacification Commissioner Dao Ban Ya and his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Annam's Li Hao led ninety thousand men along three mountain routes, broke through Ailao, invaded Laos, and killed Pacification Commissioner Dao Ban Ya and two of his sons.

sentences.zh: 其季子怕雅賽走八百，宣慰刀攬那遣兵送至景坎。

translations.literal: His youngest son Pa Ya Sai fled to Babai; Pacification Commissioner Dao Lanna dispatched troops to escort him to Jingkan.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Pa Ya Sai fled to Babai; Pacification Commissioner Dao Lanna sent troops to escort him to Jingkan.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐琮以聞，命怕雅賽襲父職，免其貢物一年，賜冠帶、彩幣，以示優恤。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qian Mu Zong reported it; Pa Ya Sai was ordered to inherit his father's post, his tribute goods were remitted for one year, and cap and sash and colored silks were bestowed to show special favor and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qian Mu Zong reported this; the court appointed Pa Ya Sai to his father's post, waived one year's tribute, and granted cap, sash, and colored silks as consolation.

sentences.zh: 既怕雅賽欲報安南之仇，覬中國發兵為助。

translations.literal: Thereafter Pa Ya Sai wished to avenge Annam and looked to China to dispatch troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Pa Ya Sai then sought revenge against Annam and hoped China would send troops to help.

sentences.zh: 帝以老撾、交阯皆服屬中國久，恤災解難，中國體也，令琮慎遣人諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor held that Laos and Jiaozhi had long submitted to China; relieving disaster and resolving difficulty was China's proper conduct, and ordered Zong carefully to dispatch persons to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that both Laos and Jiaozhi had long been subordinate to China and that aiding subjects in distress was China's duty; he ordered Zong to counsel Pa Ya Sai with care.

sentences.zh: 弘治十一年，宣慰舍人招攬章應襲職，遣人來貢，因請賜冠帶及金牌、信符。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi year 11, Pacification Commissioner designate Zhao Lan Zhang was due to inherit office; he dispatched persons to offer tribute and thereby requested bestowal of cap and sash and of gold tally and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 11 commissioner-designate Zhao Lan Zhang petitioned for succession, sent tribute, and requested cap, sash, gold tally, and credentials.

sentences.zh: 賚賞如制，其金牌、信符，俟鎮巡官勘奏至日給之。

translations.literal: Rewards were granted according to regulation; as for the gold tally and credentials, they were to be given on the day the frontier inspection officials' investigation memorial arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards followed regulation; the gold tally and credentials were to be issued once frontier officials verified his claim.

sentences.zh: 十一月，招攬章遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Zhao Lan Zhang dispatched envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhao Lan Zhang sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 吏部言：「招攬章系舍人，未授職，僭稱宣慰使，雲南三司官冒奏違錯，宜治罪。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel said: "Zhao Lan Zhang is a designate who has not yet received office; he presumptuously styled himself pacification commissioner; the Yunnan Three Offices officials rashly memorialized in error—they ought to be punished."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel said: "Zhao Lan Zhang is only a designate and has not yet been appointed; he improperly styled himself pacification commissioner, and Yunnan officials wrongly memorialized on his behalf—they should be punished."

sentences.zh: 宥之。

translations.literal: They were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: All were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，招攬章言：「交阯應襲長子光紹，為叔所逐，出亡老撾，欲調象馬送回。」

translations.literal: In Jiajing year 9, Zhao Lan Zhang said: "Jiaozhi's heir-designate eldest son Guang Shao was driven out by his uncle, fled abroad to Laos, and wishes to mobilize elephants and horses to send him back."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 9 Zhao Lan Zhang reported: "Jiaozhi's designated heir Guang Shao was expelled by his uncle, fled to Laos, and now seeks to mobilize elephants and horses to return him."

sentences.zh: 守臣言：「據招攬章之言，懼納亡之罪，且假我為制服之資，留之啟釁，遣之招兵，宜聽光紹自歸，並責其私納罪。」

translations.literal: The border officials said: "According to Zhao Lan Zhang's words, he fears the crime of harboring fugitives, and moreover would use us as resources to subdue them—keeping Guang Shao would provoke quarrels; sending him back would recruit troops; Guang Shao should be allowed to return on his own, and private acceptance should also be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Border officials replied: "Zhao Lan Zhang fears punishment for sheltering a fugitive and would use our support to restore Guang Shao—keeping him invites conflict, while sending him back would raise troops; Guang Shao should return on his own, and unauthorized acceptance should be punished."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，雲南巡撫汪文盛言：「老撾土舍怕雅聞征討安南，首先思奮，且地廣兵多，可獨當一面。

translations.literal: In year 24, Yunnan Grand Coordinator Wang Wensheng said: "The Laos local chief Pa Ya, hearing of the campaign against Annam, was first to think of exerting himself; moreover his territory is broad and his troops many—he can alone hold one front.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Yunnan Grand Coordinator Wang Wensheng reported: "Laos chief Pa Ya, hearing of the campaign against Annam, was eager to serve first; his territory is broad and his forces numerous, and he could hold one front alone.

sentences.zh: 八百、車裏與老撾相近，孟艮在老撾上流，皆多兵象，可備征討。

translations.literal: Babai and Cheli are close to Laos; Menggen is upstream from Laos—all have many troops and elephants and can be prepared for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Babai and Cheli lie near Laos, and Menggen is upstream—all have large forces and elephants and could support the campaign.

sentences.zh: 請免其察勘，就令承襲，以備征調。」

translations.literal: I request that their inspection be waived and that they immediately be allowed to succeed, so as to prepare for levy and dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that their inspection be waived and that they be appointed at once for military levy."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，土舍怕雅蘭章遣人進舞牌牙象二、母象三、犀角十，雲南守臣以聞。

translations.literal: In year 44, local chief Pa Ya Lan Zhang dispatched persons presenting two dancing-tusk elephants, three female elephants, and ten rhinoceros horns; the Yunnan border officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44 chief Pa Ya Lan Zhang sent two dancing-tusk elephants, three female elephants, and ten rhinoceros horns; Yunnan officials reported this.

sentences.zh: 禮部以非貢期，且無漢、緬公文，第來路險遠，跋涉逾年，宜受其所貢，給賞遣之，毋令赴京。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites held that it was not the tribute season and there were no Chinese or Burmese documents; yet the route was perilous and remote and the journey had taken more than a year—what they offered should be accepted, rewards given, and they dispatched, and they should not be made to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites noted that it was not tribute season and no proper documents accompanied the mission, but the route was perilous and the journey had taken more than a year; the court should accept the gifts, reward the envoys, and send them home without requiring them to come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 時緬勢方張，剪除諸部，老撾亦折而入緬，符印俱失。

translations.literal: At that time Burmese power was just rising, cutting down and eliminating the various departments; Laos too submitted and entered Burma, and tally and seal were both lost.
translations.idiomatic: Burmese power was then on the rise, subduing neighboring departments; Laos too submitted to Burma and lost its credentials and seal.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年，緬敗，老撾來歸，奉職貢，請頒印。

translations.literal: In Wanli year 26, Burma was defeated; Laos came back in submission, maintained tribute duties, and requested issuance of a seal.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 26, after Burma's defeat, Laos returned, resumed tribute, and requested a new seal.

sentences.zh: 命復鑄老撾軍民宣慰使司印給之。

translations.literal: An order was issued to recast the Laos Military-Civilian Pacification Commission seal and grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a new Laos Military-Civilian Pacification Commission seal cast and issued.

sentences.zh: 四十年貢方物，言印信毀於火，請復給，撫鎮官以聞。

translations.literal: In year 40 he offered local products, saying the seal and credentials had been destroyed by fire and requesting restoration; the frontier pacification officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 he sent tribute reporting that fire had destroyed his seal and credentials and asking for replacements; frontier officials reported this.

sentences.zh: 明年再頒老撾印。

translations.literal: The next year the Laos seal was again issued.
translations.idiomatic: The following year a new Laos seal was issued.

sentences.zh: 時宣慰猶貢象及銀器、緬席，賜予如例。

translations.literal: At that time the pacification commissioner still offered elephants, silver vessels, and Burmese mats; grants and rewards were according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner still sent elephants, silverware, and Burmese mats and received the usual rewards.

sentences.zh: 自是不復至雲。

translations.literal: From this he no longer came to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After that he no longer came to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 其俗與木邦同，部長不知姓，有三等：一曰招木弄，一曰招木牛，一曰招木化。

translations.literal: Their customs are the same as Mubang's; the chiefs do not know surnames—there are three ranks: one called Zhaomunong, one called Zhaomuniu, and one called Zhaomuhua.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs match Mubang's; chiefs use no surnames and hold three ranks: Zhaomunong, Zhaomuniu, and Zhaomuhua.

sentences.zh: 而為宣慰者，招木弄也，代存一子，絕不嗣。

translations.literal: The one who serves as pacification commissioner is the Zhaomunong; each generation keeps one son and never adopts an heir.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner is always from the Zhaomunong rank; each generation keeps one son and never adopts an heir.

sentences.zh: 其地東至水尾，南至交阯，西至八百，北至車裏，西北六十八程至雲南布政司。

translations.literal: Its territory extends east to Shuiwei, south to Jiaozhi, west to Babai, north to Cheli—sixty-eight stages northwest to the Yunnan Provincial Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory reached east to Shuiwei, south to Jiaozhi, west to Babai, and north to Cheli—sixty-eight stages northwest to the Yunnan Provincial Administration.

sentences.zh: 八百

translations.literal: Babai
translations.idiomatic: Babai

sentences.zh: 〈（二宣慰司）〉

translations.literal: (two Pacification Commissions)〉
translations.idiomatic: (two Pacification Commissions)]〉

sentences.zh: 八百，世傳部長有妻八百，各領一寨，因名八百媳婦。

translations.literal: Babai—by tradition handed down, the chief had eight hundred wives, each governing one stockade; hence the name Eight Hundred Daughters-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that Babai's chief had eight hundred wives, each ruling a stockade, hence the name "Eight Hundred Daughters-in-Law."

sentences.zh: 元初征之，道路不通而還，後遣使招附。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan they campaigned against it; the roads were impassable and they returned; afterward they dispatched envoys to summon submission.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yuan campaigns failed to reach Babai for lack of roads; later envoys secured its submission.

sentences.zh: 元統初，置八百等處宣慰司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuantong, the Babai and other places Pacification Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuantong era the Babai Pacification Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十一年，八百媳婦國遣人入貢，遂設宣慰司。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 21, the Eight Hundred Daughters-in-Law state dispatched persons to offer tribute, and the pacification commission was then established.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 21 the Eight Hundred Daughters-in-Law state sent tribute, and the pacification commission was established.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，八百土官刀板冕遣使貢象及方物。

translations.literal: In year 24, Babai tribal official Dao Ban Mian dispatched envoys offering elephants and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Babai chief Dao Ban Mian sent elephants and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，西平侯沐英遣雲南左衛百戶楊完者往八百招撫，至是來貢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Western Pacification Marquis Mu Ying had dispatched Yunnan Left Guard centurion Yang Wanzhe to Babai to summon and pacify; at this time he came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Western Pacification Marquis Mu Ying had sent Yunnan Left Guard centurion Yang Wanzhe to Babai to win submission; this tribute followed that mission.

sentences.zh: 帝諭兵部尚書茹瑋曰：「聞八百與百夷構兵，仇殺無寧日。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Minister of War Ru Wei, saying: "I hear Babai and the Baiyi are raising troops against one another, feuding and killing without a day of peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Minister of War Ru Wei: "I hear Babai and the Baiyi tribes are at war, feuding without end.

sentences.zh: 朕念八百宣慰遠在萬里外，能修職奉貢，深見至誠。

translations.literal: I reflect that the Babai pacification commissioner, far away beyond ten thousand li, can maintain tribute duties and office—this deeply shows utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Babai pacification commissioner, ten thousand li away, still maintains tribute and duty—this shows remarkable sincerity.

sentences.zh: 今與百夷構兵，當有以處之。

translations.literal: Now they are at war with the Baiyi; something must be done about it.
translations.idiomatic: They are now at war with the Baiyi, and the matter must be handled.

sentences.zh: 可諭意八百，令練兵固守，俟王師進討。」

translations.literal: You may convey our intention to Babai, ordering them to drill troops and hold firm, awaiting the imperial army's advance to chastise them."
translations.idiomatic: Convey our wishes to Babai: they should train troops and stand firm until the imperial army advances to punish the enemy.

sentences.zh: 自是及永樂初，頻遣使入貢，賜予如例。

translations.literal: From then until the early Yongle period they frequently sent envoys with tribute, and rewards followed the usual precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the early Yongle reign they sent tribute missions repeatedly, and rewards followed the established precedent.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年設軍民宣慰使司二，以土官刀招你為八百者乃宣慰使，其弟刀招散為八百大甸宣慰使，遣員外郎左洋往賜印誥、冠帶、襲衣。

translations.literal: In Yongle year 2 two Military-Civilian Pacification Commissions were established, with native official Dao Zhaoni as Babai Zhenai Pacification Commissioner and his younger brother Dao Zhaosan as Babai Greater Dian Pacification Commissioner; Court Official Zuo Yang was sent to bestow seals, patent letters, hat, sash, and formal robes.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2 two military-civilian pacification commissions were set up, appointing Dao Zhaoni as Babai Zhenai commissioner and his brother Dao Zhaosan as Babai Greater Dian commissioner; Court Official Zuo Yang was sent with seals, patents, robes, and credentials.

sentences.zh: 刀招散遣人貢馬及方物謝恩，命五年一朝貢。

translations.literal: Dao Zhaosan sent envoys offering horses and local products to express gratitude; they were ordered to present tribute once every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Zhaosan sent tribute of horses and local products in thanks; the court required tribute once every five years.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遣內官楊瑄賫敕諭孟定、孟養等部，道經八百大甸，為土官刀招散所阻，弗克進。

translations.literal: That year the inner court eunuch Yang Xuan was sent bearing edicts to instruct Mengding, Mengyang, and other domains; passing through Babai Greater Dian he was blocked by native official Dao Zhaosan and could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the palace eunuch Yang Xuan was sent with edicts for Mengding, Mengyang, and other domains, but Dao Zhaosan of Babai Greater Dian blocked his route and he could not get through.

sentences.zh: 三年遣使諭刀招散曰：「朕特頒金字紅牌，敕諭與諸邊為信，以禁戢邊吏生事擾害，用福爾眾。

translations.literal: In the third year envoys were sent to instruct Dao Zhaosan: "We have specially issued gold-letter red placards and edicts to the borderlands as credentials, to restrain border officials from provoking incidents and harassment, for the benefit of your people.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 envoys told Dao Zhaosan: "I have issued gold-letter red placards and edicts to the frontier as credentials, to stop border officials from provoking trouble and harming your people.

sentences.zh: 諸宣慰皆敬恭聽命，無所違禮。

translations.literal: All Pacification Commissioners have respectfully obeyed without breach of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: All pacification commissioners have obeyed respectfully without breach of protocol.

sentences.zh: 惟爾年幼無知，惑於小人孟乃朋、孟允公等，啟釁生禍，使臣至境，拒卻不納。

translations.literal: Only you, young and ignorant, were misled by petty men Meng Naipeng, Meng Yungong, and others, provoking trouble and disaster, and when envoys reached your border you refused and would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Only you, young and ignorant, were led astray by petty men such as Meng Naipeng and Meng Yungong, stirred up trouble, and refused to receive my envoys at your border.

sentences.zh: 廷臣鹹請興師問罪，朕念八百之人豈皆為惡，兵戈所至，必及無辜，有所不忍。

translations.literal: Court ministers all asked to raise troops to demand punishment; We reflect that not all the people of Babai are wicked—where arms reach, the innocent must suffer, and We cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The court urged war, but I reflected that not all Babai people are evil—arms inevitably harm the innocent, and I could not bear that.

sentences.zh: 茲特遣司賓田茂、推官林楨賫敕往諭，爾能悔過自新，即將奸邪之人擒送至京，庶境土可保。

translations.literal: We now specially dispatch Court Reception Officer Tian Mao and Investigating Official Lin Zhen bearing edicts to instruct you: if you can repent and reform, immediately seize the wicked men and send them to the capital, and your territory may be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: I now send Tian Mao and Lin Zhen with edicts: if you repent and reform, seize the wicked and send them to the capital, and your lands may be spared.

sentences.zh: 其或昏迷不悛，發兵討罪，孥戮不貸！」

translations.literal: If you remain deluded and unrepentant, We shall send troops to punish you, and your families will not be spared!"
translations.idiomatic: If you remain obstinate, I shall send troops to punish you, and your families will not be spared!

sentences.zh: 並敕西平侯沐晟嚴兵以待。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered the Marquis of Xiping, Mu Sheng, to hold troops in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered the Marquis of Xiping, Mu Sheng, to hold troops ready.

sentences.zh: 以馬軍六百、步軍一千四百護內官楊安、郁斌前往。

translations.literal: Six hundred cavalry and fourteen hundred infantry escorted the inner court eunuchs Yang An and Yu Bin on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred cavalry and fourteen hundred infantry escorted the palace eunuchs Yang An and Yu Bin.

sentences.zh: 又慮老撾乘車裏空虛，或發兵掩襲，或與八百為援，可遣其部長率兵一萬五千往備。

translations.literal: Fearing also that Laos might take advantage of Cheli's emptiness to raid by surprise or aid Babai, their chieftain could be ordered to lead fifteen thousand troops to guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Laos might exploit Cheli's weakness to raid or aid Babai, their chieftain was to lead fifteen thousand troops as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 三年，刀招你等遣使奉金縷表文，貢金結絲帽及方物。

translations.literal: In the third year Dao Zhaoni and others sent envoys presenting a gold-threaded memorial and offering gold-woven silk caps and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Dao Zhaoni and others sent a gold-threaded memorial with gold-woven silk caps and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝命受之，仍加賜予。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered acceptance and added further gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the tribute and added further rewards.

sentences.zh: 西平侯沐晟奏：「奉命率師及車裏諸宣慰兵至八百境內，破其猛利石厓及者答二寨，又至整線寨。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Xiping, Mu Sheng, memorialized: "Obeying orders I led troops together with Cheli pacification forces into Babai territory, captured their Menglishiya and Zheda stockades, and advanced to Zhengxian stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Sheng reported: "Leading troops with Cheli pacification forces into Babai, we took Menglishiya and Zheda stockades and advanced to Zhengxian.

sentences.zh: 木邦兵破其江下等十余寨。

translations.literal: Mobang troops captured more than ten stockades including Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Mobang troops captured more than ten stockades including Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 八百恐，遣人詣軍門伏罪。」
